evidence.description: FACT (confidence: 1.0): Firmware contains NO references to this region via FAT mount points. No sd_raw_read/write operations targeting 0x24000000-0x27FFFFFF or 0x28900000-0x2A61BDFF found in APP.bin (excluding known settings/calibration ranges).

FACT (confidence: 1.0): Binary inspection reveals FAT-like boot sector signature at 0x24007E00 and directory entries with deleted files: BOOT.bin @ 0x24028000 (12,736 bytes, 9-Dec-2022), APP.bin @ 0x2402C000 (2,576,940 bytes, 9-Dec-2022), UI-QVGA.bin @ 0x242A2000 (460,800 bytes, 5-Dec-2022).

FACT (confidence: 1.0): Settings block (0x28000000, 400 bytes) and calibration slots (0x28800000, 100x16 bytes) are written via RAW SD operations within this region, completely ignoring any FAT filesystem structures. See Finding-0009.

STRONG EVIDENCE (confidence: 0.9): SD image contains ext4 partition remnants (originally 7GB filesystem on 4GB card) and extensive garbage/junk data between known functional regions. This strongly suggests recycled SD card that was re-partitioned without full erase, rather than intentional legacy firmware design.

IMPLICATION (confidence: 1.0): RAW writes to settings/calibration will corrupt any FAT filesystem that might exist in this region. This is intentional behavior - firmware treats this entire region as RAW storage, not FAT-managed space.

provenance: Codex RAW SD access analysis (2026-01-14) + SD binary inspection
summary: Memory region 0x24000000-0x2A61BDFF contains FAT-like structures (deleted BOOT/APP/UI files) but has NO active FAT volume mount in firmware. Firmware performs RAW writes to 0x28000000 (settings) and 0x28800000 (calibration) within this region, ignoring any FAT structures. Origin uncertain: either legacy firmware remnant or recycled SD card artifacts.
title: SD Region 0x24000000-0x2A61BDFF: No Active FAT Volume
